query: Inside the Chalk Circle Word reaches Bram that you mean to empty the captain's charm. He turns up with his sleeves rolled. "Regulation hazing," he announces, "section four. You stand in the circle. I throw. You don't step out. Ready?" Hold the circle against him You don't step out. By the twentieth hex Bram is red in the face and you are still in the circle, scorched and planted. "Adequate," he says, gruffly, and doesn't put you on report. The ninth hex knocks you clean out of the circle. Bram notes it in his book. "Section four, failed," he says. "Again next week." Take it all on your shield arm You don't try to be clever. You just stand there and take it, every hex, on your arm, until Bram runs out. Your arm is purple for a week. Bram looks almost impressed. Shrug it off in the coat You button the quilted coat to the chin and plant your feet. The hexes thud into the padding like snowballs into a wall. Bram runs out first. "That's cheating," he says. "Section four doesn't mention coats," you say.
